sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and learned counsel for the State.
3.

The Petitioner are accused in G.R. Case No.19 of 2023, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C.(City), Cuttack, arising out of Badambadi UPD Cuttack P.S. Case No.13 of 2023 for commission of alleged offences under Sections 406/419/420 of IPC.
4.
Learned counsel, on instruction, submits that except the present BLAPLs, no other bail application of the Petitioners relating to the aforementioned P.S. Case is pending in any other Court.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Cuttack by order dated 16.12.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioners have been remanded in the case at hand on 10.11.2023 and charge sheet has already been filed on 15.01.2024 and taking into account that the allegation is primarily based on documentary evidence, their continuance of the Petitioners in custody is unwarranted.
7.

The allegation against the Petitioners who are the mother and son duo is that they have duped the gullible customers in the garb of providing them land and in the said guise have robbed them to the tune of Rs.15,50,000/-.
8. The same is refuted by the learned counsel for the Petitioners indicating that the allegation against them at best can be to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/-.

9. Learned counsel for the State further submits that the Petitioners are involved in commission of similar offences inasmuch as they have been cited as accused in Badambadi P.S. Cases Nos.23 & 50 of 2023.
Hence, as such the Petitioners are not entitled to be released on bail.
10. Considering the nature of allegation and the filing of the charge sheet, this Court directs the Petitioners to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.
11. Additionally, it is directed that the Petitioners shall furnish unencumbered property security to the tune Rs.10,00,000/-(Rupees ten lakhs) to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin.

12. It is further directed that one month after their release, the Petitioners shall furnish cash security to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakhs) in five equal monthly instalments, the first instalments shall be one month after the release of the Petitioners.
Learned Court in seisin is requested to fix the dates of submission of the rest of the instalments of 4 lakhs.
13. The amount so deposited shall be kept in an interest bearing account pledged in favour of the learned Court in seisin and shall abide by the final outcome of the case at hand.

14. It is apt to note here that the direction to furnish cash security is being imposed taking into account that the offence in question is an Economic offence and the Petitioners are accused of committing similar offence and also in tune with the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vrs. Central Bureau of Investigation & another, 2022 (10) SCC 16.
